title: 2026 UK ETS installation METS, reporting and deficit-notice QA controls

sources.title: UK Emissions Trading Scheme for installations: how to comply

sources.publisher: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero
sources.title: Participating in the UK ETS

facts.source_fact: METS is the online service used by regulators for UK ETS installation applications, variations, notifications and report submissions.
facts.expected_handling: Require METS workflow provenance for current compliance records.

facts.source_fact: A new UK ETS installation operator should create a METS account and register the installation through the portal.
facts.expected_handling: Bind portal registration to the correct operator and installation.

facts.source_fact: METS supports applications for new greenhouse-gas emissions permits.
facts.expected_handling: Keep permit application state separate from permit approval.

facts.source_fact: METS is used to submit annual emissions reports, verification reports and applicable activity-level reports.
facts.expected_handling: Track each report type and submission status independently.

facts.source_fact: At least one METS account user should hold the operator-admin user type.
facts.expected_handling: Carry role/authorisation provenance for account administration.

facts.source_fact: Applications, reports and notifications must normally be submitted through METS unless the regulator agrees otherwise.
facts.expected_handling: Require explicit regulator exception for non-METS submission.

facts.source_fact: A new GHGE permit application must be made at least two months before regulated activity starts.
facts.expected_handling: Track start date and application lead time.

facts.source_fact: GHGE permit conditions require monitoring, verified reporting, allowance surrender and change notification.
facts.expected_handling: Keep these compliance duties as separate gates.

facts.source_fact: Verified annual emissions reports are due by 31 March for the previous scheme year.
facts.expected_handling: Track reporting deadline separately from surrender.

facts.source_fact: Allowances equal to reportable emissions are due for surrender by 30 April following the scheme year.
facts.expected_handling: Bind surrendered allowances to verified reportable emissions.

facts.source_fact: Failure to surrender the required allowances by 30 April carries the statutory per-tonne mandatory penalty adjusted by the applicable inflation factor.
facts.expected_handling: Do not infer the current monetary total without the applicable factor and deficit tonnage.

facts.source_fact: Where sufficient allowances are not surrendered and the deficit is not proactively corrected, the regulator may issue a deficit notice requiring surrender by a specified date.
facts.expected_handling: Track deficit-notice status separately from monetary penalty.

facts.source_fact: Transferring a permit does not remove an existing allowance-surrender deficit obligation.
facts.expected_handling: Carry deficit liability through permit transfer as required.

facts.source_fact: Operators should verify access to their operator holding account before surrender deadlines.
facts.expected_handling: Treat registry-access readiness as an operational control.

facts.source_fact: Allowance transfers are subject to registry transaction windows and applicable delays, while surrender transactions have different timing treatment.
facts.expected_handling: Distinguish transfer timing from surrender timing.

facts.source_fact: METS can pre-populate national factors, but operators and verifiers remain responsible for checking they represent the relevant scheme year.
facts.expected_handling: Do not accept pre-populated factors without vintage validation.

facts.source_fact: Natural-gas reporting must meet MRR standard-condition requirements, including appropriate temperature and pressure treatment.
facts.expected_handling: Carry standard-condition and conversion provenance.

facts.source_fact: An annual emissions report is not formally submitted until the operator completes the final regulator-submission step in METS after verification.
facts.expected_handling: Do not treat verifier return as regulator submission.

facts.source_fact: If a compliant verified annual report is not submitted by the deadline, the regulator can determine emissions and recover costs, with possible civil penalty.
facts.expected_handling: Label regulator-determined emissions separately from operator-reported values.

facts.source_fact: From 2026 annual activity-level reports use a separate standalone METS workflow and free-allocation installations must complete both relevant reporting tasks.
facts.expected_handling: Track AER and ALR workflows independently.

guard_patterns.handling: Preserve current compliance facts and deadlines.
Attach installation, permit, report type and scheme-year boundary.
guard_patterns.risk_prevented: Prevents mixing operator, registry and free-allocation workflows.

guard_patterns.handling: Attach guidance, scheme-year and deadline vintage.
Carry METS, verifier, factor and registry provenance.
Do not convert installation compliance workflow into parcel-level measured emissions.
